_comment: The storefront's subject taxonomy: one bucket per thing a shopper is looking for.
This is the only place a bucket is defined. Prefixes are matched against a listing id
with underscores turned into hyphens (kidney_foodlist_pink -> kidney-foodlist-pink), so
a colourway, a serif edition or a translation inherits its parent's bucket and never
Order matters twice: a listing joins the first bucket whose prefix matches, so the more
specific prefixes come first (baby before diet-sheets), and the same order is the order
the buckets appear in the shop's chip row. check-taxonomy.py fails if a listing matches
two buckets, so an ambiguous prefix cannot sit here unnoticed.
families are the sales-report keyword families from zz_tp/scripts/families.py that roll
up into this bucket. They stay finer than the bucket on purpose: 'diverticulitis outsold
gout' is worth keeping, and it costs nothing to keep above a bucket that both feed.
The four Etsy-era categories (healthy-living, money-budgeting, moving-out, guides) are
deliberately absent. They were the sales report's groupings, and 'guides' was the
fallback for a family the report did not recognise, not a subject.

unmappedFamilies.reason: No wedding product exists or is planned; the family stays in the sales rules so historical rows still group, but it has no bucket to roll into.
families.py's own catch-all: a title that matched no keyword. A bucket for it would be the 'guides' mistake again.
